examples.ko: 할아버지는 지게에 나무를 가득 지고 내려오셨어요.
examples.en: Grandfather came down carrying a full load of wood on his jige.

examples.ko: 민속촌에서 지게를 직접 져 봤는데 생각보다 무거웠어요.
examples.en: I tried carrying a jige myself at the folk village, and it was heavier than I expected.
In the old days, farmers carried loads with a jige.
An old jige is on display at the museum.
My father put a sack of rice on the jige.

examples.ko: 지게를 진 사람이 좁은 길을 천천히 걸어가요.
examples.en: A man carrying a jige is walking slowly down the narrow road.

explain: 짐을 등에 지고 나르는 도구라서 '지게를 지다'라고 말해요. 지게로 짐을 나르는 사람은 '지게꾼'이라고 불러요. 요즘 일상에서는 거의 안 쓰고, 옛날이야기나 민속 체험, 박물관에서 만나요.
explain_en: Because it is carried on the back, you say '지게를 지다'. A person who carries loads with one is called a '지게꾼'. You rarely use it in daily life today; you meet it in old stories, folk experiences and museums.

examples.ko: 집이 지하철역 지근거리에 있어서 출퇴근이 편해요.
examples.en: My home is very close to the subway station, so commuting is easy.

examples.ko: 대통령을 지근거리에서 경호하는 일은 쉽지 않아요.
examples.en: Guarding the president at close range is not easy.

examples.ko: 병원이 지근거리에 있어서 아이가 아플 때 안심이 돼요.
examples.en: The hospital is nearby, so I feel at ease when my child is sick.

examples.ko: 지근거리의 가게만 다녀도 필요한 건 다 살 수 있어요.
examples.en: Even just visiting the shops close by, you can buy everything you need.

examples.ko: 집과 회사가 지근거리라서 점심에 집에 가요.
examples.en: My home and office are so close that I go home for lunch.
The secretary always works right next to the president.

explain: 일상에서는 '아주 가까운 곳'이라고 많이 말하고, '지근거리'는 뉴스나 글에서 자주 나와요. 보통 '지근거리에(서)' 모양으로 쓰고, 경호나 보좌처럼 사람 곁에서 일할 때도 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: In daily talk people usually say '아주 가까운 곳' (a very close place), while '지근거리' shows up more in news and writing. It is usually used as '지근거리에(서)', and it also fits jobs like guarding or assisting someone right beside them.

examples.ko: 나이가 지긋이 드신 할아버지가 자리를 양보해 주셨어요.
examples.en: An elderly grandfather gave up his seat for me.

examples.ko: 화가 나도 지긋이 참고 끝까지 들어 보세요.
examples.en: Even if you're angry, hold it in calmly and listen to the end.

examples.ko: 시험 결과가 나올 때까지 지긋이 기다리기로 했어요.
examples.en: I decided to wait patiently until the test results come out.

examples.ko: 아버지는 아무 말 없이 지긋이 기다려 주셨어요.
examples.en: My father waited patiently without saying a word.

examples.ko: 아이가 말을 끝낼 때까지 지긋이 들어 줬어요.
examples.en: I listened patiently until the child finished talking.

examples.ko: 선생님은 화내지 않고 지긋이 타일러 주셨어요.
examples.en: The teacher didn't get angry and patiently talked some sense into me.

explain: 소리가 [지그시]라서 '지그시'와 헷갈리기 쉬워요. '지긋이'는 서두르지 않고 참을성 있게 하는 모습에 써서 기다리다·참다·듣다와 잘 어울려요. '나이가 지긋이 들다'처럼 나이가 꽤 많다는 뜻으로도 써요. 눈을 감거나 지그시 힘을 주는 모습은 '지그시'를 써요.
explain_en: It sounds like [지그시], so it is easy to confuse with '지그시'. '지긋이' describes doing something patiently without hurrying and goes well with waiting, enduring and listening. It is also used in '나이가 지긋이 들다' to mean someone is fairly old. For closing the eyes or pressing gently, use '지그시'.

examples.ko: 어젯밤에 잠을 못 잤더니 머리가 지끈지끈 아파요.
examples.en: I couldn't sleep last night, so my head is throbbing.
Maybe I caught a cold; I have a throbbing headache.
As the meeting dragged on, my head started pounding.

examples.ko: 커피를 너무 많이 마셨더니 관자놀이가 지끈지끈 쑤셔요.
examples.en: I drank too much coffee, and my temples are throbbing.

examples.ko: 지끈지끈 아픈 머리를 누르며 약국에 갔어요.
examples.en: I went to the pharmacy, pressing my throbbing head.

examples.ko: 소음 때문에 머리가 지끈지끈 아프기 시작했어요.
examples.en: Because of the noise, my head started to throb.

explain: 주로 머리가 아플 때 써요. '머리가 지끈지끈 아파요'를 한 덩어리로 외우면 편해요. 같은 느낌의 동사로 '지끈거리다'도 써요.
explain_en: It is mainly used when your head hurts. It is easiest to memorize as one chunk: '머리가 지끈지끈 아파요'. The verb '지끈거리다' is used for the same feeling.

examples.en: Voice phishing methods are getting more sophisticated.
As factories become smarter, jobs are changing.
Cyberattacks have become more sophisticated, so they are hard to stop.
Our company decided to make its equipment smarter.
As technology gets smarter, security becomes more important too.
Scam methods have become more sophisticated, so be careful.

explain: 뉴스에서는 수법이나 기술이 더 똑똑하고 교묘해진다는 느낌으로 많이 나와요. 일상 대화에서는 '똑똑해지다'나 '스마트해지다'처럼 말해요. '지능화되다'로도 같은 뜻으로 써요.
explain_en: In the news it often means that methods or technology are becoming smarter and more cunning. In daily talk people say '똑똑해지다' or '스마트해지다'. '지능화되다' is also used with the same meaning.

examples.en: We learned about heliocentrism and geocentrism in science class.
Galileo supported heliocentrism.

examples.ko: 옛날 사람들은 지동설을 쉽게 믿지 못했어요.
examples.en: People in the past could not easily believe in heliocentrism.
It was later proven that heliocentrism was correct.

examples.ko: 지동설 때문에 재판을 받은 과학자도 있어요.
examples.en: There was even a scientist who was put on trial because of heliocentrism.

examples.ko: 지동설에 대한 영상을 보고 숙제를 했어요.
examples.en: I watched a video about heliocentrism and did my homework.

explain: 반대말은 '천동설'이고, 둘이 짝으로 자주 나와요. 과학이나 역사 수업에서 주로 쓰고, '지동설을 주장하다·지지하다'처럼 말해요.
explain_en: Its opposite is '천동설' (geocentrism), and the two often appear as a pair. It is mostly used in science and history lessons, as in '지동설을 주장하다' or '지동설을 지지하다'.

examples.en: General Yi Sun-sin was a commander of great strategic wit.

examples.ko: 이 드라마 주인공은 지략으로 위기를 넘겨요.
examples.en: The main character of this drama gets through crises with his wits.

examples.ko: 지략과 용기를 모두 갖춘 사람이 필요해요.
examples.en: We need someone who has both cleverness and courage.
He racked his brains and got ahead of the rival company.
Strength alone isn't enough. You need wits too.

examples.ko: 오늘 경기는 두 감독의 지략 대결이에요.
examples.en: Today's game is a battle of wits between the two managers.

explain: 머리를 써서 계획을 세우는 능력을 말하고, '지략이 뛰어나다·지략을 짜다'처럼 써요. 역사 이야기, 드라마, 스포츠 해설에서 자주 나오고, 일상에서는 '머리가 좋다'나 '꾀'라고 많이 말해요.
explain_en: It refers to the ability to plan by using your head, as in '지략이 뛰어나다' or '지략을 짜다'. It often appears in historical stories, dramas and sports commentary, while in daily life people say '머리가 좋다' or '꾀'.

examples.ko: 해 보기도 전에 지레 포기하지 마세요.
examples.en: Don't give up in advance before you even try.

examples.ko: 아직 모르는데 지레 겁먹을 필요 없어요.
examples.en: You don't know yet, so there's no need to get scared ahead of time.

examples.ko: 아이가 혼날까 봐 지레 울음을 터뜨렸어요.
examples.en: The child burst into tears before even being scolded, fearing it would happen.
I got disappointed before the results even came out.

examples.ko: 그 사람이 거절할 거라고 지레 생각했어요.
examples.en: I assumed in advance that he would refuse.
I worried in advance and couldn't sleep.

explain: 일이 일어나기도 전에 먼저 앞서서 한다는 뜻이라서 걱정, 포기, 겁먹다, 짐작하다 같은 말과 자주 써요. '미리'는 보통 중립적이지만 '지레'는 필요 이상으로 앞서간다는 느낌이 있어요.
explain_en: It means doing something ahead of time before the thing has even happened, so it often goes with worry, giving up, getting scared and guessing. '미리' is usually neutral, but '지레' feels like jumping ahead more than necessary.

examples.ko: 지레짐작으로 말하면 오해가 생길 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you speak based on a hasty guess, misunderstandings can happen.
That's just my own assumption.
Don't jump to conclusions; ask directly.
I jumped to conclusions just from my friend's expression.
A needless fight broke out because of a hasty assumption.
My assumption was wrong, and I felt embarrassed.

explain: 그냥 '짐작'과 달리 확인도 하기 전에 앞서서 추측한다는 느낌이 있어서, 보통 틀렸거나 좋지 않은 결과와 함께 나와요. '지레짐작을 하다', '지레짐작으로 판단하다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: Unlike plain '짐작' (a guess), it implies guessing before checking, so it usually appears with wrong or unhappy results. It is used as '지레짐작을 하다' or '지레짐작으로 판단하다'.

examples.en: I'm sorry I assumed things just from your face.
Don't jump to conclusions without checking.
I assumed he was angry, but he wasn't.
People easily jump to conclusions based on appearances.

examples.ko: 아직 얘기도 안 했는데 왜 혼자 지레짐작해요?
examples.en: We haven't even talked yet, so why are you assuming things on your own?
I assumed I would fail the interview and gave up.

explain: '-ㄹ 거라고 지레짐작하다'처럼 내용을 먼저 말하고 쓰는 경우가 많아요. 보통 확인하지 않고 틀리게 짐작했다는 부정적인 느낌이라서 '지레짐작하지 마세요'라고 많이 말해요.
explain_en: It is often used after stating the content, as in '-ㄹ 거라고 지레짐작하다'. It usually carries a negative feeling of guessing without checking and being wrong, so people often say '지레짐작하지 마세요'.

examples.ko: 지렛대를 쓰면 무거운 돌도 움직일 수 있어요.
examples.en: With a lever, you can move even a heavy stone.
We learned the principle of the lever in science class.

examples.ko: 이 사업을 성공의 지렛대로 삼고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to use this business as a lever for success.

examples.ko: 지렛대 끝을 아래로 누르니까 돌이 올라왔어요.
examples.en: When I pushed the end of the lever down, the stone came up.
The longer the lever is, the less force you need.

examples.ko: 아이는 막대기를 지렛대 삼아 바위를 밀어 봤어요.
examples.en: The child used a stick as a lever and tried pushing the rock.

explain: 실제 도구뿐 아니라 '무언가를 이루기 위한 발판'이라는 비유로도 많이 써요. 뉴스나 경제 이야기에서 '성장의 지렛대'처럼 자주 나와요.

phrases.example: 이번 성공을 지렛대 삼아 해외로 나갈 거예요.
phrases.en: use as leverage; use as a stepping stone
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 결과나 상황을 이용해서 다음 목표로 나아간다는 뜻이에요. 사업이나 뉴스에서 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means using a result or situation to move toward the next goal. It is common in business and news.
phrases.en_equiv: use X as a stepping stone

explain_en: Besides the real tool, it is often used figuratively for something that helps you achieve a goal. In news and economic talk it appears often, as in '성장의 지렛대' (a lever for growth).

examples.ko: 건강의 비결은 잘 자는 것이라는 게 제 지론이에요.
examples.en: My firm belief is that the secret to health is sleeping well.
Grandfather's principle was 'Always eat breakfast.'

examples.ko: 그는 오랜 지론을 끝까지 굽히지 않았어요.
examples.en: He never gave up his long-held belief to the end.

examples.ko: 저는 제 지론대로 매일 아침 산책해요.
examples.en: I take a walk every morning, in line with my own conviction.

examples.ko: 사장님 지론에 따르면 사람이 가장 중요해요.
examples.en: According to the boss's firm view, people are the most important.

examples.ko: 이건 어디까지나 제 지론이니까 참고만 하세요.
examples.en: This is just my own view, so take it as a reference only.

explain: 오랫동안 믿고 지켜 온 자기만의 생각을 말할 때 써요. 그냥 '생각'보다 신념에 가까워서 '제 지론은 ~예요'처럼 말하면 조금 격식 있고 단단한 느낌이 나요.
explain_en: It is used for your own idea that you have believed in and kept for a long time. It is closer to a conviction than plain '생각', so saying '제 지론은 ~예요' sounds a bit formal and firm.

examples.en: I walked very carefully, as if crossing a minefield.

examples.ko: 이 회의는 말 한마디가 지뢰밭 같아요.
examples.en: In this meeting, every single word feels like a minefield.
That topic is a minefield for our family.

examples.ko: 지뢰밭이 있던 곳이 지금은 공원이 되었어요.
examples.en: The place where the minefield used to be has become a park.
Talk about dating is a minefield, so don't bring it up.
In an interview, every question feels like stepping into a minefield.

explain: 실제 땅 이름으로도 쓰지만, 건드리면 문제가 생기는 위험한 주제나 상황을 비유할 때 더 자주 들려요. 같은 비유로 실수로 민감한 부분을 건드렸을 때 '지뢰를 밟았다'고도 말해요.
explain_en: It can name a real area, but you more often hear it as a metaphor for a risky topic or situation where touching the wrong thing causes trouble. In the same metaphor, people say '지뢰를 밟았다' when they accidentally touch a sensitive point.

examples.ko: 팀이 지리멸렬해서 경기를 제대로 못 했어요.
examples.en: The team was in disarray, so it couldn't play the game properly.

examples.ko: 발표 내용이 지리멸렬하면 듣는 사람이 지쳐요.
examples.en: If the content of a presentation is disjointed, listeners get tired.

examples.ko: 회의가 지리멸렬하게 이어져서 결론이 안 났어요.
examples.en: The meeting dragged on in a scattered way, so no conclusion was reached.

examples.ko: 이야기가 지리멸렬한 영화는 끝까지 보기 힘들어요.
examples.en: A movie with a disjointed story is hard to watch to the end.
There was criticism that the government's response was chaotic.

examples.ko: 계획이 지리멸렬해 보여서 다시 짜기로 했어요.
examples.en: The plan looked disorganized, so we decided to redo it.

explain: 조직, 계획, 이야기가 갈래갈래 흩어져서 체계가 없을 때 쓰는 딱딱한 말이에요. 일상 대화에서는 '엉망이다'나 '뒤죽박죽이다'라고 더 많이 말하고, 비판하는 글이나 뉴스에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It is a stiff word for when an organization, plan or story is scattered and has no structure. In daily talk people more often say '엉망이다' or '뒤죽박죽이다', and this word appears often in critical writing and the news.

examples.en: Many applicants flocked to this open recruitment.
Applicants, please send your résumé by email.
Students aiming for medical school are attending cram schools.

examples.ko: 지망자 수가 작년보다 두 배로 늘었어요.
examples.en: The number of applicants has doubled compared with last year.
The interviewer asked the applicant a question.
We are recruiting people who want to join the drama club.

explain: '지원자'와 비슷하지만 일상에서는 '지원자'가 더 흔해요. '지망자'는 '의대 지망자'처럼 어떤 학과나 직업을 목표로 하는 사람을 말할 때 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: It is similar to '지원자', but '지원자' is more common in daily life. '지망자' fits when talking about people aiming at a certain field or job, as in '의대 지망자' (medical school aspirant).

examples.en: This brand is well known overseas.

examples.ko: 그 배우는 아직 지명도는 낮지만 연기를 잘해요.
examples.en: That actor is not well known yet, but he acts well.
We started advertising to raise our name recognition.
We invited a well-known writer to the event.
Compared with how famous he is, his skill is ordinary.

examples.ko: 지명도만 믿고 준비를 소홀히 하면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You shouldn't neglect preparation by relying only on your fame.

explain: 사람, 회사, 브랜드의 이름이 얼마나 알려졌는지를 말하고 '지명도가 높다·낮다·올리다'처럼 써요. '인지도'도 비슷하게 쓰고, 뉴스나 업무 이야기에서 자주 들려요.
explain_en: It describes how well known the name of a person, company or brand is, used as '지명도가 높다', '지명도가 낮다' or '지명도를 올리다'. '인지도' is used in a similar way, and both are common in the news and business talk.

examples.en: The branch manager went on a business trip to headquarters today.
Our branch manager is changing next month.
He was promoted to branch manager in Seoul.
We have to report to the branch manager first.
There is a company dinner to welcome the new branch manager.

examples.ko: 지사장과 본사 임원이 회의를 하고 있어요.
examples.en: The branch manager and a head-office executive are in a meeting.

explain: 본사에 대한 지사, 곧 지역 사무소의 책임자를 말해요. 직함이라서 말할 때는 '지사장님'으로 높여 불러요. 은행이나 가게의 분점 책임자는 보통 '지점장'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It refers to the head of a branch office as opposed to the head office. Because it is a job title, people address the person as '지사장님' to show respect. The head of a bank or shop branch is usually called '지점장'.
